# Offline cryptographic fixtures

These are public test vectors, never user wallet material. Test phrases are
derived from public all-zero entropy in process memory only. Transaction tests
use fabricated nonexistent inputs, block network connections and never broadcast.

`sources.json` pins upstream commits, source SHA-256 values, fixture SHA-256
values and extraction descriptions. The pinned source bytes were compared with
the originals used for extraction. Upstream license notices are in `licenses/`.

- `ecdsa.json`: 2,020 valid BitcoinJS secp256k1 deterministic signatures, including
  recovery IDs. The signing tests also exercise the four invalid private keys.
  The file's other invalid verification/recovery and extra-entropy cases are
  retained for provenance; this suite does not claim coverage of those cases.
- `rfc6979-nist.json`: all 50 prime-curve signatures from RFC 6979 A.2.3–A.2.7
  (P-192/224/256/384/521; SHA-1/224/256/384/512; `sample` and `test`). Expected
  `r` and `s` are transcribed from the standard, not generated by elliptic.
- `elliptic-issue-321.json`: the published P-224/SHA-256 invalid-signature
  example from the advisory's reference issue. Both elliptic and OpenSSL reject
  it. The array-length handling for this message-digest case was already present
  in upstream 6.6.1; the local patch corrects the separate generated-nonce path.
- `bip32.json`: BIP32 test vectors 1–4, all 17 derivation paths, including the
  leading-zero cases. Nexa has distinct network version bytes; tests compare
  the remaining BIP32 payload against the standard xprv/xpub payload.
- `bch-schnorr.json`: 12 BCH Schnorr verification vectors (five valid, seven
  invalid). This is the BCH/Nexa algorithm, **not BIP340**. A separate test
  verifier uses Noble point arithmetic and SHA-256 and is itself checked against
  all 12 vectors. It is never included in production code.
- `nexa-padding.json`: the official Nexa signature test whose `r` starts with a
  zero byte; also tests the transaction signer's little-endian hash convention.
- `p521-leading-zero-baseline.json`: three locally derived regression messages,
  indexed 194, 211 and 275 in `Altbase offline P521 nonce regression N`, with the
  public P-521 scalar from RFC 6979 A.2.7 and SHA-512. The original elliptic DER
  signatures were recorded before patching; the expected compact signatures
  came from Noble. Tests reconstruct the original one-line implementation,
  reproduce its discrepancy, then independently recompute the corrected result.
  Original signatures still verify: the demonstrated issue is nonce derivation,
  not a demonstrated recovery of a private key.

The CKB cached-cell and JoyID WebAuthn envelopes are locally constructed protocol
fixtures around these public test scalars. They are not official chain consensus
vectors and do not establish acceptance of live transactions.
